items.front: Gandhi in South Africa — years & first body?
items.back: 1893–1914 (Dada Abdulla case); founded Natal Indian Congress & newspaper 'Indian Opinion'; birthplace of Satyagraha.
items.examPoint: South Africa stint & birth of Satyagraha (1893–1914)

items.back: First Indian satyagraha; against forced indigo (Tin-Kathia), Bihar; joined peasant unrest to the national movement.
items.examPoint: Champaran Satyagraha 1917 (indigo, Tin-Kathia) — first Civil Disobedience

items.back: Kheda = first no-tax satyagraha (Patel emerges); Ahmedabad Mill Strike = Gandhi's first fast-unto-death (Anasuya Sarabhai).
Against the Rowlatt (Sedition Committee) Act; Gandhi used the Home Rule League network — his first all-India act.
1920–22; combined Punjab wrong + Khilafat + Swaraj; withdrawn after Chauri Chaura (Feb 1922).
items.examPoint: Non-Cooperation Movement 1920–22 — programme, spread, new institutions

items.back: 12 March – 6 April 1930 (Sabarmati → Dandi); launched the Civil Disobedience Movement.

items.front: Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) — what did it give?
items.back: Withdrew ordinances, released non-violent prisoners, allowed coastal salt; Congress joined 2nd RTC. NO police-excess enquiry.
items.examPoint: Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) contents & the police-excess-enquiry exclusion

items.back: With Ambedkar; reserved seats for Depressed Classes replaced separate electorates (Communal Award).
8 Aug 1942, Bombay; 'Do or Die'; Gandhi detained at Aga Khan Palace, Pune.
Instrumental in abolishing indentured labour (1917); after Salt Law (1930) the INC was declared illegal.
items.examPoint: Gandhi's roles — abolition of indentured labour, 1918 War Conference recruitment, INC declared illegal

items.back: Indian Opinion, Young India, Navajivan, Harijan; Hind Swaraj (1909), My Experiments with Truth, Songs from Prison.
items.examPoint: Gandhi's writings & newspapers (Young India, Navajivan, Harijan, Hind Swaraj, Songs from Prison) & titles (Mahatma-Tagore, Father of Nation-Bose)

items.front: Who gave 'Mahatma' and 'Father of the Nation'?
items.back: 'Mahatma' by Rabindranath Tagore; 'Father of the Nation' popularised by Subhas Chandra Bose.
items.examPoint: Titles 'Mahatma' & 'Father of the Nation'; INC Belgaum session 1924

items.back: Rests on Truth (Satya) + Non-violence (Ahimsa); pure ends need pure means (Hind Swaraj, 1909).

items.front: Gandhi's one INC presidency & his death?
items.back: Presided only at Belgaum (1924); assassinated 30 Jan 1948 by Nathuram Godse (Martyrs' Day).
Tanguturi Prakasam ('Andhra Kesari'), Konda Venkatappayya, Pattabhi Sitaramayya; poet Garimella Satyanarayana.
items.examPoint: Gandhi & Andhra — visits, khadi, Andhra role in movements
